topic: How do GEO vs LEO satellite orbits affect latency and coverage in hybrid networks for rural substation monitoring?
response: GEO satellites offer large stationary footprints, leading to higher latency due to longer propagation delays. LEO satellites have lower latency (less than 1 second) and smaller footprints, but their coverage is less extensive. Hybrid networks leveraging both GEO and LEO offer global coverage with varying latency depending on location and network configuration.
reference_context: Satellite communication systems provide seamless wireless coverage, complementing terrestrial networks.  Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites are gaining research interest due to their potential for global data access and enhanced rates. They offer lower latency than GEO satellites and can reach remote areas with limited infrastructure.
